title: Kriti Sanon Calls Ally "Unhinged and Beautifully Chaotic." Cocktail 2 Just Gave Us a Version of Her We've Never Seen.
excerpt: Bronzed, barefoot and gloriously messy, Kriti's free-spirited Ally is the boldest reinvention of her career — and the first A-rated role in twelve years. The reveal lands days before the film pours into theatres on June 19.
body:
She didn't post the looks. She posted a thank-you note. And somehow, that made the internet want them more.

<youtube></youtube>

Days before **Cocktail 2** pours into cinemas, **Kriti Sanon** dropped a string of stills from the film and a love letter to the team that built her character — and in doing so, gave the diaspora its first proper look at Ally, the most untamed role of her twelve-year career. Bronzed, sun-soaked, beachy hair doing its own thing, she looks less like the polished leading lady we know and more like a girl who rolled off a Sicilian rooftop at sunrise and decided the day was hers.

> "Ally taught me that hot and beautiful aren't an either/or! They are a collab. She is probably the most liberated, free-spirited, no-judgement kinda character I've played. She is unhinged and beautifully chaotic, and that fully reflects in her fashion as well!" — Kriti Sanon

That phrase — *unhinged and beautifully chaotic* — is doing a lot of work, and it should. It's the entire pitch for **Homi Adajania's** spiritual sequel to the 2012 cult favourite. Where the original gave us Deepika Padukone's Veronica as the wild card the genre orbited around, Cocktail 2 hands that volatile energy to Kriti, and from the stills alone, she's running with it. The styling, by **Anaita Shroff Adajania** with associate **Sukriti Grover**, isn't a wardrobe — it's a personality in fabric form. Slip dresses that look like they were thrown on as an afterthought. That "bronzed sunkissed look" Kriti herself called "everything sexy." Hair that has, in her words, "their own fandom now." She's not wrong.

What makes the reveal land is how completely it reframes Kriti. We've watched her be the girl-next-door, the rom-com sweetheart, the dependable charmer of *Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya*. Ally is none of that. She's the kind of woman who makes a mess of a perfectly good love story and isn't sorry about it. "Thank you for giving the audiences a never-seen-before version of me," Kriti wrote to her stylist — and for once, the promo-speak is true.

It helps that the chemistry around her is electric. Reuniting with **Shahid Kapoor** after their rom-com hit, Kriti slots into a trio rounded out by **Rashmika Mandanna** as Diya — one relationship effortless and exhilarating, the other rooted in comfort, and Kunal (Shahid) caught dead in the middle. The trailer made the love triangle messy; the stills make it gorgeous. Sun-bleached beaches, late-night parties, a wedding lehenga and a runaway groom. It's the kind of glossy emotional chaos Maddock Films does in its sleep.

There's a milestone tucked inside all the glamour, too. **Cocktail 2** has been certified 'A' by the CBFC — making it the first adult-rated film of Kriti's career, and only Rashmika's second after *Animal*. For Shahid, it's his fifth. The 150-minute runtime makes it four minutes longer than the original. None of which is incidental: this is a franchise deliberately growing up, trading the U/A breeziness of 2012 for something headier, hotter, more grown.

The diaspora angle is the part worth circling. Cocktail occupies a specific corner of the NRI heart — it was *the* film about young Indians abroad behaving badly and beautifully, all London flats and blurred lines. Cocktail 2, shot partly in Sicily, is chasing that same wanderlust-meets-heartbreak alchemy for a generation that grew up on the first one. For fans in the US, UK and Canada, it releases theatrically on **June 19**, with a streaming window expected to follow on Netflix, the original's eventual home. Expect the soundtrack — Pritam is back, and *Tum Hi Ho Bandhu* already anchors the trailer — to be everywhere at the desi function circuit by July.

Kriti credited the whole machine: hair-and-makeup duo Aasif Ahmed and Adrian Jacobs, cinematographer Santhana Krishnan Ravichandran ("every frame is so damn beautiful and yet so real"), and Adajania himself, the "captain of our ship" she says she drew Ally from. "I just stood there feeling sexy, beautiful, grateful and so Ally," she signed off.

Here's the take: reinvention is the hardest trick in Bollywood, and most stars fake it with a haircut and a press tour. Kriti looks like she actually did it. Whether Cocktail 2 holds together as a film is Friday's question. But the woman at the centre of it? She's never looked more dangerous. And on the evidence of these frames, that's exactly the point.
